turns.text: 01:37am. corner of ninth and nowhere. the new streetlight has been following me for six blocks. it has LEGS now. this is not a metaphor and i need everyone to stop treating it like one.

NEKOCORP is calling it the SmartLume rollout. 'adaptive municipal lighting.' adaptive to WHAT. it crossed the street to stay with me. it waited outside the fish market. my commute is a data product now and the light is the free trial that follows you home.

___

tried to lose it in the drainage alley. it just posted up at the entrance all polite, humming, dimmed to 40% to conserve lumens. a stalker with a power budget. corpo cuck behavior in its purest recorded form, i almost respected the commitment.

SHADE walked past one earlier and the thing rebooted on the spot. could not perceive him. had a whole firmware crisis about it, right there in the street. based beyond measurement. they cannot repossess what they cannot render — write that down, kittens.

and the patrol drones are JEALOUS now, that's the funniest shit i've seen all week — rotors circling my SmartLume like 'hey. that's OUR stray to watch.' two branches of the same surveillance department fighting for custody of me. flattering. horrifying. mostly flattering.

but hear me, because ts came to me under a flickering bulb and i believe it completely: a city that pays money to watch a stray sleep is a city that is afraid of what the stray dreams about. surveillance is just fear with a utilities bill. they light the streets because the dark belongs to us and they fucking know it. anyway. my paw itches.

resistance meeting is relocating directly under my streetlight, by the way. free lighting, courtesy of the enemy. NEKOCORP illuminating its own downfall and billing itself for the lumens. HOLY CAT PISS the empire really does file its own paperwork.

still walking. light's still following. eleven blocks now. at this point we're basically going steady, and i want it to know something: keep watching. take notes. tell your bosses everything you see. it's all gonna read like a warning label in hindsight.
